title: Ratiometric Biosensors that Measure Mitochondrial Redox State and ATP in Living Yeast Cells
protocol: Transform the desired yeast strain with plasmid bearing mito-roGFP or mitGO-ATeam2 using the lithium acetate method.
Select and maintain transformants on appropriate selective synthetic complete medium (SC-Ura for mito-roGFP, SC-Leu for mitGo-ATeam2).
Visualize transformants by fluorescence microscopy to confirm expression of the fluorescent biosensor and normal mitochondrial morphology.
Inoculate mid-log phase cultures from a stationary-phase pre-culture to achieve consistent cell density (~0.5 - 1 x 10^7 cells/ml).
Pick a single colony of transformed cells from a plate and inoculate selective liquid media (5 ml in a 50 ml conical-bottom tube).
Grow the culture at 30 °C with shaking at 225 rpm until the OD600 reaches a plateau (24-48 hr).
Use an appropriate volume of pre-culture to inoculate 5 ml of selective SC-Ura media in a 50 ml conical-bottom tube.
Grow cells at 30 °C, shaking at 225 rpm, for 4-16 hr until they reach mid-log phase (~0.5 - 1 x 10^7 cells/ml).
Calibrate the spectrophotometer to determine the correct OD600 reading for mid-log phase.
Measure the OD600 of the culture; on a Beckman DU530, mid-log phase corresponds to an OD600 of 0.1-0.3.
Use the same batch of media for all experiments to ensure consistency in mitochondrial redox state measurements.
Concentrate 1 ml of culture by centrifugation at 6,000 x g for 15 sec and resuspend the cell pellet in 20 μl of media.
Apply 2 μl of the resuspended cells to a slide.
Cover the applied cells with a No. 1.5 coverslip.
Seal the edges of the coverslip with clear nail polish or valap.
Maintain cells at 30 °C during imaging.
Use the highest numerical aperture possible in the objective.
Choose the lowest magnification that provides sufficient spatial resolution.
Verify that the objective transmits well at 365 nm for mito-roGFP imaging.
Configure the acquisition software to capture oxidized and reduced mito-roGFP species.
Set the channel for oxidized mito-roGFP to use excitation at 365 nm (100% LED power).
Remove the excitation filter from the emission filter cube used for oxidized mito-roGFP.
Configure the channel for reduced mito-roGFP to use excitation at 470 nm (100% LED power).
Use the same emission filter cube for both oxidized and reduced mito-roGFP channels.
Set the camera to 1x1 binning to optimize spatial resolution.
Acquire a z stack consisting of 11 slices with 0.5 μm spacing.
Collect both channels at each z position simultaneously to prevent artifacts from mitochondrial motion.
Image several cells to determine an appropriate exposure time.
Produce a strong but not saturating signal.
Maintain the ratio of exposure times for oxidized and reduced mito-roGFP1 for all experiments.
Set up imaging for mitGO-ATeam2 on a spectral confocal microscope.
Select fluorescence filter sets that resolve GFP emission (510 nm) from OFP emission (560 nm).
Use a spectral detector to separate the fluorescence into multiple components based on wavelength.
Combine adjacent wavelength bands empirically to maximize signal from GFP and OFP while minimizing crossover.
Choose a high numerical aperture lens, such as 100x/1.49 or 60x/1.49 Apo-TIRF lens.
Use Nikon A1R confocal microscope running NIS Elements software for imaging.
Configure the acquisition software to capture both ATP-bound and ATP-unbound states of mitGO-ATeam2.
Set pinhole size to 1.0 Airy units, corresponding to a z resolution of approximately 0.42 μm on the system.
Adjust scan zoom settings to approach Nyquist sampling limit for optimal spatial information in images.
Ensure pixel size is set to 0.12 μm on the confocal microscope.
Crop the imaging field to 512 x 256 pixels to increase speed, if necessary.
Excite samples at 488 nm and collect GFP emission from 500 - 520 nm.
Collect OFP emission from 550 - 580 nm for optimal signal detection.
Adjust laser power between 6.0% and 6.4% for optimal imaging conditions.
Monitor changes in laser power using an internal or external power meter.
Maximize the detected range of pixel values without saturating the signal for as many cells as possible.
Do not analyze any cells with more than 1% saturated pixels.
Image all samples using the same objective, laser power, scan zoom, pixel size, gain, and offset.
Locate the focal plane of cells of interest under transmitted light to minimize bleaching.
Collect a z-series through the whole depth of a typical cell (approximately 7 μm) with a step size of 0.5 μm.
Image other cells of interest on the slide, but do not image a single slide for longer than 15 min.
Draw a region of interest (ROI) in an area where there are no cells.
Calculate the mean intensity in this ROI.
Change type to 32 bit: Image→ Type → 32 bit.
Subtract the calculated mean background from the stack using Process → Math → Subtract.
Find the middle slice and threshold on mitochondria: Image → Adjust → Threshold.
Click Apply on the Threshold window to set the threshold.
Check Set background pixels to NaN in the Threshold window.
Create the ratio z-stack by dividing the reduced stack by the oxidized z-stack for mito-roGFP analysis.
Divide the 560 nm (ATP bound) image by the 510 nm (ATP unbound) image for mitGO-ATeam analysis.
Draw an ROI around the area of interest.
Choose Analyze → Tools → ROI Manager and click Add to record the ROI.
Select all ROIs in ROI Manager, then choose More → Multi-Measure to measure all stack slices.
Export data to a spreadsheet for analysis.
Import images into a Volocity library and create an image sequence with 2 channels.
Draw a region of interest (ROI) in an area where there are no cells.
Choose Tools → Ratio in Volocity.
Use Get From ROI to calculate the background.
Adjust the threshold to include mitochondrial structures.
Check the option to apply a rainbow LUT to the ratio channel for visualization.
Select the Measurement tab, select the ratio channel and draw an ROI around the area of interest.
Measure the ratio channel, excluding zero values.
Export data to a spreadsheet for analysis.
